chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) and Ali (peace be upon him) used to send their Hady (sacrificial animal) from Medina, then they would enter the state of Ihram. And if they sent it from one of the far horizons, they would appoint their companions to tie the Hady and shear its hair on a known day, then they would restrain themselves on that day until the Day of Nahr (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah) - from everything that the Muhrim restrains himself from, and they would avoid everything that the Muhrim avoids, except that he does not say the Talbiyah except for the one who is a Hajj or an Umrah.

key_terms.إِشْعَارِهِمَا: Shearing the hair of the Hady
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram
key_terms.يَتَجَرَّدَانِ: They would enter Ihram (free from clothing restrictions)
key_terms.يَوْمِ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What were the specific ritual practices of Ibn Abbas and Ali regarding Hady and Ihram prohibitions?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the scholarly practice of Ibn Abbas and Ali (peace be upon them) in performing Hajj al-Tamattu' or Qiran, where they would dispatch their sacrificial animal (Hady) from Medina or other regions before entering the state of Ihram. It emphasizes their strict adherence to Ihram prohibitions, with the notable exception of the Talbiyah, which is reserved specifically for those performing Hajj or Umrah, reflecting the nuanced legal distinctions in Shia jurisprudence regarding ritual purity and sacrifice.
